  • Habit Correctors: Easy-to-wear appliances that help correct poor oral habits that can affect jaw growth, such as thumb sucking or prolonged pacifier use.
  • Orthodontics and Palatal Expansion: Gentle appliances and devices to encourage proper jaw development and alignment.
  • Orthotropics®: The “Gold Standard” facial growth guidance approach. Orthotropics encourages the jaws to grow “up and out” in the face, improving jaw development and airway health.

Hi there! I'm a bike messenger by day, aspiring actor by night, and this is my website. I live in Los Angeles, have a great dog named Jack, and I like piña coladas. (And gettin' caught in the rain.)

...or something like this:

The XYZ Doohickey Company was founded in 1971, and has been providing quality doohickeys to the public ever since. Located in Gotham City, XYZ employs over 2,000 people and does all kinds of awesome things for the Gotham community.

item.title: Privacy Policy
item.dc:creator: tntadmin
item.content:encoded:
Who we are

Suggested text: Our website address is: https://www.newteethhouston.com/blog.

Comments

Suggested text: When visitors leave comments on the site we collect the data shown in the comments form, and also the visitor’s IP address and browser user agent string to help spam detection.

An anonymized string created from your email address (also called a hash) may be provided to the Gravatar service to see if you are using it. The Gravatar service privacy policy is available here: https://automattic.com/privacy/. After approval of your comment, your profile picture is visible to the public in the context of your comment.

Media

Suggested text: If you upload images to the website, you should avoid uploading images with embedded location data (EXIF GPS) included. Visitors to the website can download and extract any location data from images on the website.

Cookies

Suggested text: If you leave a comment on our site you may opt-in to saving your name, email address and website in cookies. These are for your convenience so that you do not have to fill in your details again when you leave another comment. These cookies will last for one year.

If you visit our login page, we will set a temporary cookie to determine if your browser accepts cookies. This cookie contains no personal data and is discarded when you close your browser.

When you log in, we will also set up several cookies to save your login information and your screen display choices. Login cookies last for two days, and screen options cookies last for a year. If you select "Remember Me", your login will persist for two weeks. If you log out of your account, the login cookies will be removed.

If you edit or publish an article, an additional cookie will be saved in your browser. This cookie includes no personal data and simply indicates the post ID of the article you just edited. It expires after 1 day.

Embedded content from other websites

Suggested text: Articles on this site may include embedded content (e.g. videos, images, articles, etc.). Embedded content from other websites behaves in the exact same way as if the visitor has visited the other website.

These websites may collect data about you, use cookies, embed additional third-party tracking, and monitor your interaction with that embedded content, including tracking your interaction with the embedded content if you have an account and are logged in to that website.

Who we share your data with

Suggested text: If you request a password reset, your IP address will be included in the reset email.

How long we retain your data

Suggested text: If you leave a comment, the comment and its metadata are retained indefinitely. This is so we can recognize and approve any follow-up comments automatically instead of holding them in a moderation queue.

For users that register on our website (if any), we also store the personal information they provide in their user profile. All users can see, edit, or delete their personal information at any time (except they cannot change their username). Website administrators can also see and edit that information.

What rights you have over your data

Suggested text: If you have an account on this site, or have left comments, you can request to receive an exported file of the personal data we hold about you, including any data you have provided to us. You can also request that we erase any personal data we hold about you. This does not include any data we are obliged to keep for administrative, legal, or security purposes.

Where your data is sent

Suggested text: Visitor comments may be checked through an automated spam detection service.

item.title: Welcome to Our Blog!
item.dc:creator: New Teeth Dental Solutions
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to the brand-new blog for Dr. Brad Jetton and New Teeth Dental Solutions of Houston! We hope you check back to this page regularly to learn something new about oral hygiene, dental treatments, and how to keep your smile looking and feeling its best for a lifetime!

Meet Dr. Jetton

Dr. Brad Jetton was born and raised in Wichita Falls, where he knew early-on he wanted to pursue a career in dentistry. In addition to being fascinated by treating and caring for teeth, he also liked the idea of getting to know new and interesting people in the process!

After earning his bachelor's degree in biology at Midwestern State University and his Doctor of Dental Surgery from the University of Texas Dental Branch (now called the UT Health Houston School of Dentistry). He also proudly completed the American Academy of Implant Dentistry’s Maxicourse to provide top quality dental implant treatment right here in the office!

About Our Practice

In addition to offering a variety of tooth replacement options, Dr. Jetton and the team are pleased to be a full-service general dentistry practice, including treatments like preventive exams and cleanings, dental crowns and fillings, cosmetic dentistry, Invisalign, and emergency dentistry. We even offer sedation options to help keep you feeling calm and comfortable during any treatment!

We’re also proudly dental insurance friendly, welcome flexible financing, run frequent special offers, and have our own in-house membership plan for those who don’t have private dental insurance and want to save money on routine care.

Why Choose Us?

While we know that you have plenty of options for protecting your smile in the Houston area, we believe our caring, compassionate dental team stands out in the crowd.

First, because Dr. Jetton is skilled in a variety of dental treatments, you won’t need to ‘shop around’ for emergency services, cosmetic upgrades, or beautiful, lifelike restorations like dental implants.

Furthermore, between our friendly staff, gentle dentist, and sedation options, we are pleased to offer a more relaxed, comfortable dental experience, no matter which treatment you need.

Finally, with our insurance friendliness, flexible financing options, money saving special offers, and valuable in-housed membership program, we can protect you and your family’s smiles more affordably than you may have realized!

For details about any of our treatments, schedule a consultation with Dr. Jetton today, and to learn more about how to safeguard your smile and protect your teeth and gums for a lifetime, don’t forget to check back regularly right here on our blog. We can’t wait to see you soon!

item.title: Orthodontic Inquiry: Can I Get Invisalign After Braces?
item.dc:creator: New Teeth Dental Solutions
item.content:encoded:
You might think of your overcrowded, crooked, or gapped teeth as aesthetic concerns, but these issues can also detract from your dental health. For example, it can be harder to brush and floss thoroughly when some enamel surfaces are inaccessible, or you might develop a bite misalignment that results in a sore, stiff, or locked jaw.

Your dentist can help straighten your smile with Invisalign, but if you’ve completed treatment with braces in the past, you might wonder if you’re an eligible candidate for this service. Continue reading to learn more about why there’s still hope!

Why Did My Teeth Shift Later in Life?

If you’ve had an evenly spaced grin for most of your life, only natural to wonder why your teeth would have shifted out of place later on, especially if you had braces as a youth. But this can happen for various reasons, such as:

  • Neglecting orthodontic instructions. If you fail to wear your retainer as directed after finishing braces, your teeth are more likely to shift back to their original positions.
  • Arrival of wisdom teeth. These 3rd molars notoriously shift neighboring teeth out of alignment when they grow in, which can be problematic if they show up after you’ve already completed your orthodontic service.
  • Daily wear and tear. The pressure placed on them when you bite and chew every day can push them out of their ideal places over time.
  • Other habits. You might also develop misalignments if you clench your teeth together subconsciously during the day or overnight.

How Does Invisalign Work?

Unlike braces, which rely on bulky metal brackets and wires, this service utilizes a series of removable, transparent trays. They’re customized to fit snugly over your arches and exert consistent, gentle pressure to move your teeth to their proper positions.

But you must wear these clear aligners for 20 to 22 hours daily to prevent potential relapse. Then, after about a week or two, you’ll be directed to switch to the next pair of trays in your series, which accounts for the ongoing movement of your smile.

Can I Get Invisalign After Having Braces?

If you’re worried that you’re too old for Invisalign or that you’re not qualified for treatment if you had braces at some point in your life, you can thankfully set your concerns aside. Generally, your age and previous dental work aren’t the deciding factors that determine whether you’re a good candidate for this service.

Eligibility for this alternative orthodontic option is usually based on other factors, such as whether your mouth is healthy, the severity of the misalignments, and whether you can comply with wear-time guidelines and other treatment requirements.

If you’re still unsure whether Invisalign is right for you, the best way to find out is to schedule an appointment with your dentist!

Meet the Author

Dr. Brad Jetton has over 15 years of experience helping patients build and maintain beautiful, healthy teeth and gums. He earned his Doctor of Dental Surgery from the University of Texas Dental Branch (now the UT Health Houston School of Dentistry), and remains committed to continuing education to stay abreast of the most up-to-date treatments and technology. Today, he offers a complete menu of services, including Invisalign, to meet your unique needs under one roof. If you need to straighten your smile, you can request an appointment on the website or call the office at (713) 257-9470.
